How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

Below is a step‑by‑step guide to build the **RESTful GET request** that will return the *Speed* information for a specific interface on a Cisco Nexus Dashboard (ND) instance. | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **ND IP** | `192.120.45.67` | | **API version** | `6.3.1` | | **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | **Query parameters** | `fabricName=Network1`
`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | > **Note** – The API expects the *interfaceType* value in **lower‑case** (`ethernet`). > The *infoType* value is also case‑sensitive (`Speed`). --- ## 1. Full URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` --- ## 2. Example `curl` command ```bash curl -k \ -u : \ # Basic Auth – replace with your creds -H "Accept: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` * `-k` – skip certificate verification (use only in test environments). * Replace `` and `` with your ND credentials. * If ND uses token‑based auth, add `-H "Authorization: Bearer "` instead of `-u`. --- ## 3. Example Python `requests` snippet ```python import requests url = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" params = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } # Basic Auth auth = ("", "") # Or token auth # headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer "} response = requests.get(url, params=params, auth=auth, verify=False) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` > **Tip** – In production, set `verify=True` and provide the proper CA bundle. --- ## 4. Using the provided `functions.requests_get` helper If you’re working inside the environment that exposes the `functions.requests_get` wrapper, you can call it like this: ```python from functions import requests_get result = requests_get( url="https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", params={ "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } ) print(result) ``` > The wrapper will handle the HTTP GET internally; just make sure you’ve authenticated (e.g., via environment variables or a session object) before calling it. --- ## 5. What to expect in the response A successful call returns JSON similar to: ```json { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed", "speed": "1000000000" // 1 Gbps, for example } ``` If the interface isn’t found or the parameters are wrong, you’ll receive an error code (e.g., `404 Not Found` or `400 Bad Request`) with a descriptive message. --- ### Quick Checklist | ✅ | Item | |----|------| | ✅ | Use HTTPS and the correct base URL. | | ✅ | Include all required query parameters. | | ✅ | Use the correct case for `interfaceType` and `infoType`. | | ✅ | Authenticate (Basic Auth or Bearer token). | | ✅ | Verify the response status code before parsing. | That’s it! You now have a fully‑formed RESTful request to fetch the speed of an Ethernet interface on your Cisco Nexus Dashboard.
